Apple fertilizer schedule and orchard dose calculator

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Bearing standard apple trees (10 years and older) need about 700 g N, 350 g P₂O₅ and 700 g K₂O plus 70–100 kg FYM per tree per year; younger trees get 70 : 35 : 70 g and 10 kg FYM per year of age (Dr. YSP UHF Nauni, SKUAST-K). Mature M.9 high-density trees need about 120–180 g N, 50–80 g P₂O₅ and 150–250 g K₂O per tree through weekly drip (ICAR-CITH, Dr. YSP UHF). Give FYM, phosphorus and half the potash in November–December, 60% of nitrogen before bud break and the rest after petal fall.

Apple fertilizer calculator

Enter your orchard in bigha, kanal, nali or acre, the tree age and spacing. The calculator works out the tree count, the dose per tree, total SSP, MOP and urea (or CAN in acidic soil), bags to buy, and when to give each part. For M.9 on drip it gives weekly MAP, urea and SOP.

Calculator rules (research reference, section 17): standard dose 70 : 35 : 70 g × age up to 10 years, FYM 10 kg × age; M.9 dose 35 : 17.5 : 35 g × age up to 7 years, capped at 245 g N per tree; soil test ±25% (ICAR-IISS brackets); off-year or excess shoots halve or remove the post-bloom nitrogen; pH below 5.5 switches urea to CAN; M.9 drip: all phosphorus as MAP, all potash as SOP, urea reduced by MAP's nitrogen, 15 weekly doses mid-March to June; warning above SKUAST-K's 120 kg N/ha Karewa ceiling.

In acidic soil (pH below 5.5) use CAN or lime/dolomite rather than ammonium sulphate alone.

When to apply

WhenWhat
Late autumn (Nov–Dec)All FYM, all phosphorus (SSP) and 50–100% of potash (MOP), in a ring 30 cm inside the drip line, never touching the trunk
Pre-bloom (Feb–Mar, 2–3 weeks before bud break)50–67% of nitrogen (urea or CAN)
After petal fall (Apr–May)The remaining 33–50% of nitrogen and any remaining potash, only if fruit set is heavy. In an off year cut this nitrogen by 50–100% so trees do not throw wild shoots
Fruit sizing (Jun–Aug)No heavy soil nitrogen; SOP (0:0:50) and calcium sprays
Leaf fall (Oct–Nov)3–5% urea (30–50 g/L) + 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.1–0.2% Solubor on green leaves before they drop: reloads next spring's buds and speeds rotting of scabbed leaves (SKUAST-K)

Worked example: 5 bighas (1 acre) in Himachal, standard trees, year 8

6 × 6 m spacing gives 112 trees (about 22 per bigha). Soil: pH 5.3 (acidic), organic carbon 1.1%, N 260 (low, +25%), P 15 (medium), K 105 (low, +25%), heavy bloom. Year-8 dose: N 560 × 1.25 = 700 g, P₂O₅ 280 g, K₂O 700 g per tree: 78.4 kg N, 31.4 kg P₂O₅ and 78.4 kg K₂O per acre, plus about 9 tonnes FYM.

ProductQuantityWhen
SSP (16%)196 kg (about 4 bags)Nov–Dec
MOP (60%)131 kg (about 2.6 bags)65 kg Nov–Dec, 65 kg Apr–May
CAN (25% N), because pH is below 5.5314 kg (about 6.3 bags)188 kg Feb–Mar, 125 kg Apr–May

Because pH is 5.3, check lime or dolomite with your soil lab, and add the pink-bud boron, 4–6 calcium chloride sprays and the October urea-zinc-boron spray.

Worked example: 8 kanals (1 acre) in Kashmir, M.9 high density, year 5

3.0 × 1.5 m gives 899 trees. Dose 175 : 87.5 : 175 g per tree = 157 kg N, 79 kg P₂O₅, 157 kg K₂O and about 13.5 tonnes FYM. Through drip in 15 weekly doses (mid-March to end of June): MAP 129 kg, SOP 315 kg and urea 308 kg in total, that is 8.6 kg MAP + 21.0 kg SOP + 20.6 kg urea per acre per week. Watch shoot length (30–45 cm is right) and trim June nitrogen if shoots go past 50 cm.

Foliar sprays: boron, calcium, zinc, magnesium

NutrientWhenSprayWhy
BoronPink bud and October0.1–0.15% Solubor or boric acid (1–1.5 g/L); never above 0.2%Pollen tube growth; reduces flower drop
Calcium4–6 sprays, 15 days apart, from 2–3 weeks after petal fall0.3–0.5% calcium chloride (3–5 g/L); skip above 28–30°CPrevents bitter pit and cork spot
ZincDelayed dormant and October0.5% zinc sulphate (5 g/L) + 0.25% limeLittle leaf and rosettes
MagnesiumWalnut stage1–2% magnesium sulphate (10–20 g/L)Prevents early yellow leaf drop
PotassiumFruit sizing1% SOP (10 g/L)Size and colour (ICAR-CITH)

Tank mixing: never mix calcium chloride or calcium nitrate with sulphates (SOP, magnesium, zinc sulphate) or phosphates (MAP, MKP, 19:19:19). Use separate tanks.

Biofertilizers and biostimulants

  • VAM (AMF) + Trichoderma + Pseudomonas strongly reduced replant disease deaths (SKUAST-K 2024).
  • Humic acids improve fine roots in compacted soil when combined with drainage and mulch; they cannot cure root rot.
  • Seaweed (Ascophyllum) and amino acids support fruit set and colour under cold spring swings, alongside boron and calcium (Scientia Horticulturae).

Mistakes that waste money

  • Water-soluble fertilizer poured on waterlogged or very acidic soil is mostly wasted.
  • Excess growth regulators on stressed trees worsen fruit drop.
  • Full nitrogen in an off year produces long shoots, shade and more alternate bearing.

Questions farmers ask

How much fertilizer does an apple tree need?

Standard trees: 70 g N, 35 g P₂O₅, 70 g K₂O and 10 kg FYM per year of age until year 10, then 700 : 350 : 700 g and 70–100 kg FYM. M.9 trees: half that per year of age up to year 7.

When should I give fertilizer to apple trees?

FYM, phosphorus and half the potash in November–December; 60% of nitrogen 2–3 weeks before bud break; the rest after petal fall if fruit set is good.

What is the best fertilizer for apple trees?

Well-rotted FYM plus balanced N, P and K by tree age, with boron, calcium and zinc sprays. Use CAN instead of urea in acidic soil.

Which spray is given to apple in October?

3–5% urea + 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.1–0.2% Solubor on green leaves before leaf fall (SKUAST-K).

How do I calculate fertilizer for my apple orchard in bigha or kanal?

Use the calculator above: 1 acre = 5 Himachal bighas = 8 J&K kanals = 20.16 Uttarakhand nalis.
